issues.body: `open_object` indexes `blocks`, then marks the separately supplied `root.block_id` visited and traverses `root` directly without proving that the indexed block with that ID exists and is canonically identical. An attacker/caller can remove the real root from `blocks`, insert any unique same-object extra block to preserve `blocks.len() == root.chunk_count`, and pass the original root separately. Traversal visits the external root plus all authenticated descendants, so `visited.len() == chunk_count` and opening succeeds even though `blocks` is not exactly the object's block set. This contradicts the public API and SKILL claims that the root is included and every extra/missing block is rejected.
issues.fix_hint: Before traversal, require `index.get(&root.block_id)` to exist and require that indexed envelope to equal the supplied root (or compare its canonical encoding/digest and all relevant fields), then traverse that indexed value. Add a regression test that removes `blocks[0]`, inserts a unique same-object extra envelope to keep the declared count, passes the original root separately, and asserts rejection. Also cover the same-block-id/different-envelope variant.
issues.title: open_object accepts a root that is absent from the claimed exact block set

verdict.summary: The Merkle traversal and tamper checks are generally well structured and the disclosure remains appropriately research-grade, but the public `open_object` API does not enforce its load-bearing exact-set invariant: the separately supplied root need not actually be one of `blocks`. This permits an unrelated extra block to replace the root in the supplied set while verification still succeeds. The tests are non-vacuous for many mutation classes, but their helper always derives the root from `blocks[0]`, so they do not cover this API-level mismatch.
